p.src: Meanwhile, Yuan Shao had stationed his army in Henei, where provisions were running short. Han Fu, Governor of Jizhou, sent men with grain to supply the army. The adviser Feng Ji said to Yuan Shao, “A true man ranges freely across the realm. Why should he wait for another to send him food? Jizhou is rich in money and grain. Why do you not seize it, General?” Yuan Shao replied, “I have no good plan.” Feng Ji said, “Secretly send a messenger with a letter to Gongsun Zan, urging him to invade Jizhou and proposing that you attack it together. He will certainly raise an army. Han Fu is a man without strategy; he will surely ask you to assume the government of the province. Then you may seize your opportunity, and the province will fall into your hands with no more effort than spitting into your palm.” Yuan Shao was delighted and at once dispatched a letter to Gongsun Zan. When Gongsun Zan read that they were to attack Jizhou together and divide its territory equally, he rejoiced and raised his army that very day. Yuan Shao, however, secretly sent a man to warn Han Fu. Alarmed, Han Fu summoned his two advisers, Xun Chen and Xin Ping, to deliberate. Xun Chen said, “Gongsun Zan is leading the hosts of Yan and Dai in a headlong advance. Their onset cannot be withstood. Moreover, Liu Bei, Guan Yu, and Zhang Fei are assisting him, so resistance will be difficult. Yuan Benchu surpasses other men in wisdom and courage and commands a great many renowned generals. You should invite him to govern the province with you. He will surely treat you generously, and then Gongsun Zan need cause you no concern.” Han Fu immediately sent his Assistant Officer Guan Chun to invite Yuan Shao. Geng Wu, the Chief Clerk, remonstrated: “Yuan Shao is a solitary guest with an exhausted army, dependent upon our every breath. He is like an infant held in the palm: cut off its milk, and it will starve at once. Why would you entrust the affairs of the province to him? This is to lead a tiger into a flock of sheep.” Han Fu replied, “I was once a subordinate of the Yuan clan, and my abilities are inferior to Benchu’s. The ancients chose the worthy and yielded their positions to them. Why are you gentlemen jealous?” Geng Wu sighed, “Jizhou is finished!” Thereupon, more than thirty men resigned their posts and departed. Only Geng Wu and Guan Chun lay in ambush outside the city to await Yuan Shao. Several days later, Yuan Shao arrived at the head of his army. Geng Wu and Guan Chun rushed out with drawn swords, intending to assassinate him. Yuan Shao’s general Yan Liang instantly cut down Geng Wu, while Wen Chou slew Guan Chun. Yuan Shao entered Jizhou, appointed Han Fu General Who Displays Might, and divided the province’s administration among Tian Feng, Ju Shou, Xu You, and Feng Ji, stripping Han Fu of all authority. Han Fu’s regrets came too late. Abandoning his wife and children, he rode alone to seek refuge with Zhang Miao, Governor of Chenliu.

p.src: Now when Gongsun Zan learned that Yuan Shao had already occupied Jizhou, he sent his younger brother Gongsun Yue to demand a share of its territory. Yuan Shao said, “Ask your brother to come himself, and I shall discuss the matter with him.” Gongsun Yue took his leave and set out for home. Before he had gone fifty li, a troop suddenly burst from beside the road, shouting, “We are retainers of Chancellor Dong!” A storm of arrows shot Gongsun Yue dead. His attendants escaped and returned to Gongsun Zan, reporting that Gongsun Yue was dead. Gongsun Zan raged, “Yuan Shao lured me into raising an army against Han Fu, while he seized the prize from within. Now he has even disguised his men as Dong Zhuo’s troops and shot my brother dead. How can I leave this wrong unavenged?” He mobilized every soldier under his command and drove toward Jizhou. Learning that Gongsun Zan’s army was approaching, Yuan Shao likewise led out his forces. The two armies met at the Pan River: Yuan Shao’s army stood east of the bridge, and Gongsun Zan’s west of it. Gongsun Zan reined his horse upon the bridge and shouted, “Faithless wretch! How dare you betray me?” Yuan Shao also spurred his horse to the bridge and, pointing at Gongsun Zan, said, “Han Fu lacked ability and willingly yielded Jizhou to me. What concern is that of yours?” Gongsun Zan said, “In former days, believing you loyal and righteous, we raised you up as leader of the alliance. But your conduct now reveals the heart of a wolf and the behavior of a cur. How can you show your face in this world?” Furious, Yuan Shao cried, “Who will capture him?”

p.src: Before the words had left his mouth, Wen Chou spurred his horse, leveled his spear, and charged straight onto the bridge. Gongsun Zan engaged Wen Chou beside the bridge. Before they had fought more than ten bouts, Gongsun Zan could resist no longer and fled in defeat. Wen Chou pressed his advantage and pursued. Gongsun Zan fled into his battle lines, but Wen Chou galloped straight into the center, charging back and forth among the troops. Four valiant generals under Gongsun Zan came forward together to meet him. With a single thrust Wen Chou knocked one general from his horse, and the other three fled. Wen Chou chased Gongsun Zan clear beyond the formation, and Gongsun Zan fled toward a mountain valley. Urging his horse onward, Wen Chou roared, “Dismount at once and surrender!” Gongsun Zan had dropped both bow and arrows, and his helmet had fallen to the ground. His hair streaming loose, he drove his horse around the hillside. His horse stumbled on its forelegs, and Gongsun Zan was pitched down the slope. Wen Chou hastily gripped his spear and moved in for the kill. Suddenly a young general wheeled out from the left of the grassy slope, galloped forward with leveled spear, and charged straight at Wen Chou. Gongsun Zan scrambled back up the slope and looked at the youth: he stood eight chi tall, with thick brows, large eyes, a broad face, and a strong double chin, and bore an awe-inspiring presence. He fought Wen Chou for fifty or sixty bouts, yet neither could gain the advantage. When Gongsun Zan’s relief force arrived, Wen Chou turned his horse and withdrew. The young general did not pursue him. Gongsun Zan hurried down the earthen slope and asked the youth his name. The youth inclined his body and replied, “I am from Zhending in Changshan. My surname is Zhao, my given name Yun, and my style Zilong. I was formerly a man under Yuan Shao’s command. But when I saw that he had no heart to remain loyal to the sovereign and save the people, I left him expressly to join your command. I never expected to meet you here.” Gongsun Zan was overjoyed. Together they returned to camp and set the troops and armor in order.

p.src: The next day, Gongsun Zan divided his cavalry and infantry into left and right wings. There were more than five thousand horses, most of them white. Because Gongsun Zan had once fought the Qiang people and always chosen white horses for his vanguard, he was known as the “White Horse General.” The Qiang would flee at the mere sight of white horses, and so his army possessed a great many of them. Yuan Shao appointed Yan Liang and Wen Chou as vanguard commanders, each leading a thousand archers and crossbowmen, and likewise divided them into left and right wings. He ordered those on the left to shoot at Gongsun Zan’s right wing, and those on the right to shoot at his left. He further ordered Qu Yi to lead eight hundred archers and fifteen thousand infantrymen and form up in the center. Yuan Shao himself commanded several tens of thousands of cavalry and infantry in support at the rear. Since Gongsun Zan had only just gained Zhao Yun and did not yet know whether he was truly loyal, he ordered him to command a separate force in the rear. He sent his general Yan Gang forward as the vanguard. Gongsun Zan himself commanded the center and sat his horse upon the bridge. Before him stood a great red banner, bordered in gold, bearing the character “Commander.” The drums sounded from the hour of the dragon until the hour of the serpent, but Yuan Shao’s army did not advance. Qu Yi ordered all his archers to lie concealed behind their arrow-shields and loose only when they heard the signal gun. Yan Gang’s troops raised a clamor and charged straight at Qu Yi. Seeing them approach, Qu Yi’s soldiers remained prone and motionless. Only when the enemy had drawn very near did a gun sound, and all eight hundred archers and crossbowmen discharged their weapons at once. Yan Gang hastily turned back, but Qu Yi spurred his horse, brandished his blade, and cut him down beneath his mount. Gongsun Zan’s army was utterly defeated. The left and right wings tried to come to the rescue, but Yan Liang and Wen Chou held them back with their archers and crossbowmen. Yuan Shao’s forces advanced together and fought their way straight to the Boundary Bridge. Qu Yi arrived on horseback, first slew the standard-bearer, and hacked down the embroidered banner. Seeing the embroidered banner fall, Gongsun Zan turned his horse, descended from the bridge, and fled. Qu Yi led his troops in a charge straight into the rear guard, where he encountered Zhao Yun, who leveled his spear, urged on his horse, and charged directly at him. Within only a few bouts, Zhao Yun thrust Qu Yi from his horse with a single stroke of his spear. Zhao Yun rode alone into Yuan Shao’s army, charging left and right as though no one stood before him. Gongsun Zan led his forces back into the attack, and Yuan Shao’s army suffered a great defeat.

p.src: Now Yuan Shao had first sent scouts to observe the fighting. They returned to report that Qu Yi had slain the enemy commander, seized his standard, and was pursuing the routed troops; so he made no preparations and rode out to watch with Tian Feng, several hundred halberdiers from his personal guard, and a few dozen mounted archers. Laughing heartily, he said, “Gongsun Zan is a man of no ability!” Even as he spoke, Zhao Yun suddenly charged up before him. The archers hurried to shoot, but Zhao Yun speared several of them in succession, and the whole force fled. From behind, Gongsun Zan’s troops surged forward and encircled them on every side. In alarm Tian Feng said to Yuan Shao, “My lord, take shelter for the moment inside that empty wall!” Yuan Shao dashed his helmet to the ground and cried, “A true man would rather face the foe and die in battle! How could he crawl behind a wall in hope of saving his life?” His soldiers united in a desperate fight, and Zhao Yun could not break through. Then the main body of Yuan Shao’s army swept up, while Yan Liang also arrived with his troops, and the two forces attacked together. Zhao Yun protected Gongsun Zan and hacked a path through the close encirclement, returning to Jie Bridge. Yuan Shao drove his troops onward and pursued them back across the bridge; those who fell into the water and died were beyond counting. Yuan Shao led the pursuit. Before he had gone five li, a tremendous shout arose behind the hills, and a powerful body of troops swept into view, headed by three great warriors: Liu Xuande, Guan Yunchang, and Zhang Yide. While in Pingyuan, they had learned of the struggle between Gongsun Zan and Yuan Shao and had come expressly to lend aid. Now the three horses and three different weapons came flying forward, straight at Yuan Shao. Yuan Shao was terrified out of his wits. His precious sword fell from his hand beneath his horse, and he hastily wheeled about and fled, while his followers fought desperately to rescue him across the bridge. Gongsun Zan likewise gathered his army and returned to camp. When Xuande, Guan, and Zhang had finished asking after him, Gongsun Zan said, “Had you not come from afar to rescue me, Xuande, I should nearly have met with disaster.” He then had Zhao Yun presented to them. Xuande esteemed and cherished him greatly, and already felt reluctant to part from him.

p.src: Now Yuan Shao, having lost the engagement, held his position firmly and would not come out. The two armies faced each other for more than a month, until someone went to Chang’an and reported the matter to Dong Zhuo. Li Ru said to Dong Zhuo, “Yuan Shao and Gongsun Zan are both heroes of the present age. They are now fighting at the Pan River. You should issue a decree in the Emperor’s name and send men to reconcile them. Grateful for your favor, they will surely submit to the Grand Preceptor.” Dong Zhuo was delighted. The next day he sent Grand Tutor Ma Midi and Grand Coachman Zhao Qi to carry the decree thither. When the two reached Hebei, Yuan Shao went a hundred li to welcome them and received the decree with repeated bows. The next day the two envoys went to Gongsun Zan’s camp and proclaimed the imperial instructions. Gongsun Zan then sent a messenger with a letter to Yuan Shao, and the two sides negotiated peace; the envoys themselves returned to the capital to report the fulfillment of their mission. That very day Gongsun Zan withdrew his army and also submitted a memorial recommending Liu Xuande as Chancellor of Pingyuan. When Xuande parted from Zhao Yun, they clasped hands and shed tears, unable to bear leaving each other. Zhao Yun sighed and said, “Formerly I mistakenly took Gongsun Zan for a hero; but judging by his conduct now, he is merely another of Yuan Shao’s kind!” Xuande said, “For the present, humble yourself and serve him. The day will come when we meet again.” They parted with tears.

p.src: When Sun Jian received the letter, he said, “That intolerable Liu Biao! Once he cut off my road home. If I do not seize this chance to avenge that wrong, when shall I?” He summoned Cheng Pu, Huang Gai, Han Dang, and the others under his command to deliberate. Cheng Pu said, “Yuan Shu is full of deceit. His word cannot yet be trusted.” Sun Jian replied, “I myself wish to avenge the wrong. Why should I count on Yuan Shu’s aid?” He promptly sent Huang Gai ahead to the riverbank to prepare warships, load them with weapons and provisions, and place the horses aboard the larger vessels; then he fixed a day to raise the army. Spies on the river learned of these preparations and went to report them to Liu Biao. Greatly alarmed, Liu Biao urgently assembled his civil and military officers to deliberate. Kuai Liang said, “There is no need for concern. Order Huang Zu to lead the troops of Jiangxia as the vanguard, while you, my lord, command the forces of Jingzhou and Xiangyang in support. After crossing river and lake to reach us, how can Sun Jian fully employ his martial strength?” Liu Biao approved. He ordered Huang Zu to make preparations and then raised the main army behind him.

p.src: Now Sun Jian had four sons, all born to Lady Wu. The eldest was named Ce, with the courtesy name Bofu; the second was named Quan, with the courtesy name Zhongmou; the third was named Yi, with the courtesy name Shubi; and the fourth was named Kuang, with the courtesy name Jizuo. Lady Wu’s younger sister became Sun Jian’s second wife and likewise bore him a son and a daughter. The son was named Lang, with the courtesy name Zao’an; the daughter was named Ren. Sun Jian also adopted a son from the Yu family, named Shao, with the courtesy name Gongli. Sun Jian had a younger brother named Jing, with the courtesy name Youtai. As Sun Jian was about to depart, Sun Jing led the sons to bow in a row before his horse and remonstrated: “Dong Zhuo now monopolizes power, the Emperor is weak, all within the seas is in chaos, and each strongman dominates his own region. Jiangdong has only just gained a little peace. It is not fitting to raise a great army over a trifling grudge. I beg you, elder brother, to consider it carefully.” Sun Jian said, “Brother, say no more. I mean to range unchecked across the realm. How can I leave an enmity unavenged?” His eldest son Sun Ce said, “If Father is determined to go, I wish to accompany you.” Sun Jian consented. He and Sun Ce boarded the ships and drove toward Fancheng. Huang Zu had concealed archers and crossbowmen along the riverbank. When he saw the ships draw near shore, they all loosed their arrows in a wild volley. Sun Jian ordered his men not to move rashly but to lie hidden in the ships as they passed back and forth to lure the enemy into shooting; for three days running, the ships approached the shore dozens of times. Huang Zu’s troops thought of nothing but shooting, until their arrows were exhausted. Sun Jian then pulled from his ships the arrows that had struck them, some hundred thousand or more. That day the wind was favorable, and Sun Jian ordered all his soldiers to shoot together. The troops on shore could not hold out and had no choice but to retreat.

p.src: Sun Jian’s army landed. Cheng Pu and Huang Gai divided their troops into two columns and advanced straight upon Huang Zu’s camp. Behind them Han Dang drove the troops vigorously forward. Attacked from three sides, Huang Zu suffered a crushing defeat, abandoned Fancheng, and withdrew into Dengcheng. Sun Jian ordered Huang Gai to guard the ships, while he personally led the troops in pursuit. Huang Zu led out his army to meet him and drew up his formation in the open country. Sun Jian arrayed his forces and rode out beneath the gate banner. Sun Ce, too, was fully armed and armored, holding his spear as he sat his horse beside his father. Huang Zu brought forward two officers: Zhang Hu of Jiangxia and Chen Sheng of Xiangyang. Flourishing his whip, Huang Zu cursed them loudly: “You rats from Jiangdong! How dare you invade the territory of a kinsman of the House of Han!” He then ordered Zhang Hu to issue a challenge. From Sun Jian’s formation Han Dang rode out to meet him. The two horsemen crossed weapons and fought for more than thirty bouts. When Chen Sheng saw Zhang Hu weakening, he galloped forward to aid him. Sun Ce saw him, steadied the spear in his hand, drew his bow, and set an arrow to the string. His shot struck Chen Sheng squarely in the face, and Chen Sheng fell from his horse at the twang of the bowstring. Zhang Hu was startled to see Chen Sheng fall. Caught unprepared, he received a stroke from Han Dang’s blade that sliced away half his skull. Cheng Pu spurred his horse straight before the enemy formation to seize Huang Zu. Huang Zu cast aside his helmet and warhorse, mingled with the foot soldiers, and fled for his life. Sun Jian fell upon the routed troops and pursued them as far as the Han River, then ordered Huang Gai to bring the ships forward and moor them on the Han.

p.src: Huang Zu rallied his defeated troops and went to see Liu Biao, reporting in full that Sun Jian's might was irresistible. Alarmed, Liu Biao summoned Kuai Liang to discuss the matter. Kuai Liang said, “We have just suffered defeat, and the soldiers have no heart for battle. Our only course is to deepen the moats and raise the ramparts, thereby avoiding the edge of their assault, while secretly sending someone to seek aid from Yuan Shao. Then the siege will naturally be lifted.” Cai Mao said, “Zirou's proposal is nothing but a clumsy stratagem. With the enemy at the city walls and their forces almost upon the river, how can we fold our hands and await death? Though I possess little talent, I ask leave to lead the army out of the city and settle the matter in one battle.” Liu Biao granted his request. Cai Mao led more than ten thousand troops out of Xiangyang and drew them up at Mount Xian. Sun Jian drove his victorious army onward in a sweeping advance. Cai Mao rode forth. Sun Jian said, “That man is the elder brother of Liu Biao's second wife. Who will capture him for me?” Cheng Pu spurred out with his iron-spined spear and engaged Cai Mao. Before they had fought more than a few bouts, Cai Mao turned and fled. Sun Jian drove his great army forward, slaughtering the enemy until corpses lay across the fields. Cai Mao escaped into Xiangyang. Kuai Liang declared that Cai Mao had rejected sound counsel and thereby brought about a crushing defeat, and by military law deserved beheading. But Liu Biao, having recently married Cai Mao's younger sister, refused to punish him.

p.src: Meanwhile, Sun Jian divided his forces on four sides, surrounded Xiangyang, and attacked it. Suddenly one day a furious wind sprang up and snapped the staff of the commander’s banner in the central camp. Han Dang said, “This is no auspicious omen. We should withdraw for a time.” Sun Jian said, “I have won battle after battle, and Xiangyang will be ours within days. How could I abruptly abandon the campaign merely because the wind has broken a flagstaff!” Thus he rejected Han Dang's advice and pressed the siege ever more fiercely. Kuai Liang said to Liu Biao, “Last night I observed the heavens and saw a general's star about to fall. Judging by the region of the heavens concerned, the omen must fall upon Sun Jian. My lord, you should swiftly send a letter to Yuan Shao and ask for his aid.” Liu Biao wrote the letter and asked who dared break through the encirclement and carry it out. The valiant officer Lü Gong at once volunteered to go. Kuai Liang said, “Since you dare undertake it, heed my plan. I shall give you five hundred cavalrymen, including many skilled archers. Break through their lines and head directly for Mount Xian. The enemy will surely lead troops in pursuit. Send a hundred men up the mountain to gather stones and make ready, and conceal another hundred armed with bows and crossbows in the woods. When the pursuers arrive, do not flee straight onward. Wheel and turn along a winding course, drawing them into the ambush, where arrows and stones are to be loosed together. If you gain the victory, fire a rapid succession of signal cannon, and the troops in the city will come out to support you. If no one pursues, do not fire the cannon; simply hasten on your journey. The moon will not be very bright tonight, so you may leave the city at dusk.”

p.src: Lü Gong received the plan and prepared his men and horses. At dusk, the east gate was secretly opened, and he led his troops out of the city. Sun Jian was in his tent when he suddenly heard shouting. He swiftly mounted and led more than thirty horsemen out of camp to investigate. A soldier reported, “A body of troops has fought its way out and is heading toward Mount Xian.” Without assembling his generals, Sun Jian set off in pursuit with only his thirty-odd riders. Lü Gong had already laid ambushes above and below amid the tangled mountain woods. Sun Jian's horse was swift; he came on alone, leaving his foremost men not far behind. Sun Jian shouted, “Stop! Do not flee!” Lü Gong reined about and engaged Sun Jian. After only one exchange on horseback, Lü Gong fled and slipped into a mountain path. Sun Jian pursued him inside, but Lü Gong had vanished. Just as Sun Jian was about to ascend the mountain, a gong suddenly sounded; stones came pelting down from above, while a storm of arrows flew at once from the woods. Struck by stones and arrows, Sun Jian's brains burst forth, and both rider and horse died there within Mount Xian. He was only thirty-seven years old.

p.src: Lü Gong cut off the thirty horsemen and killed them all, then fired a rapid succession of signal cannon. From the city, Huang Zu, Kuai Yue, and Cai Mao led troops out by separate routes, throwing all the Jiangdong forces into confusion. Huang Gai heard the shouts shaking the heavens and led the naval forces into the fray, meeting Huang Zu head-on. Before two bouts had passed, he captured Huang Zu alive. Cheng Pu, guarding Sun Ce, was urgently seeking a way through when he encountered Lü Gong. Cheng Pu spurred forward, and before they had fought more than a few bouts, he thrust Lü Gong from his horse with a single spear stroke. The two armies fought a great battle until dawn, when each side withdrew its troops. Liu Biao's forces returned to the city. When Sun Ce returned to the Han River, he learned that his father had been killed by the hail of arrows and that Liu Biao's soldiers had already carried the body into the city. He burst into loud weeping. The whole army wailed and wept. Sun Ce said, “With my father's body still there, how can I return home?” Huang Gai said, “We have captured Huang Zu alive. Let one man enter the city to negotiate peace, and exchange Huang Zu for our lord's body.” Before he had finished, the military officer Huan Jie stepped forth and said, “I have an old acquaintance with Liu Biao. I am willing to enter the city as envoy.” Sun Ce consented. Huan Jie entered the city, met Liu Biao, and explained the whole matter. Liu Biao said, “Wentai's body has already been placed here in a coffin. Release Huang Zu at once; let both houses cease hostilities and never again encroach upon each other.” Huan Jie bowed his thanks and was about to depart when Kuai Liang stepped forth below the stairs and cried, “No! No! I have a proposal that will ensure not one armored man of the Jiangdong armies returns alive. First behead Huan Jie, and then carry out my plan.” Indeed:
